bullets.text: CR was 92.5; auto June CR slightly elevated; CL CR in the 80s; Property CR just under 100 including 7.5 pts intangible amortization, or 92 excluding it (about 85 in June).
NPW +13% aided by controlling interest in ARX; auto organic growth hit ~10% in June; CL achieved mid-teen double-digit growth; Agency auto premium growth showed early improvement.

Introduced Platinum bundled home-and-auto product with ASI for Texas agents; rolled out new product model featuring refined segmentation, "Robinson" customer enhancements, and point-of-sale estimated Snapshot discounts.

Direct and Agency policy counts are all but equal in a "policy equinox." Progressive favors neither channel, and continues executing an agenda focused on improving Agency production and agent Snapshot adoption.

Direct auto policies in force grew 7% year-over-year, with average premiums contributing materially to progression. Agency auto showed a notable directional shift in new business, leaving Agency and Direct policy counts all but equal.

State hot spots like Texas exist, but the aggregate outlook for needed rate changes is assessed as very low, providing confidence that current market momentum is not in short-term danger of being slowed.

The $20B+ investment portfolio returned 1% YTD on a fully taxable equivalent basis. A short duration strategy mitigated declining unrealized gains from rising interest rates, though quarterly unrealized losses reduced comprehensive income.

Commercial Lines is enjoying the best of times with mid-teen growth and combined ratios in the 80s, but Progressive fully expects these results to become more consistent with long-term targets over time.

Catastrophe losses rose a little over last year, but the quarter proved very manageable with acceptable results. Significant weather events in Texas contributed to state-level variation and created a hot spot.

Uncertain economic conditions, headlined by Greece and Puerto Rico, led to significant volatility. Progressive welcomed higher interest rates and views potential Federal Reserve rate increases as a favorable force for future growth.
